features.summary: WebRender gained support for drawing and clipping along vector paths, including smoother anti-aliased edges and better hit testing, bringing more SVG shapes and CSS `clip-path` effects into its accelerated rendering. It also reworked backdrop filters—the effects that sample and blur or otherwise transform what is behind an element—to draw the needed background directly rather than copying it through extra intermediate steps. Other changes improve gradient color handling, iframe embedding policy checks, and rendering reliability in unusual or very large cases.

features.summary: Firefox’s support information now gives more detail about the display color profile used for color management, making it easier to understand how colors are adjusted for a screen. A small QCMS optimization also streamlines conversion of color values to 8-bit channels.

features.summary: Graphics IPC now gives each layer tree its own identifier namespace, reducing the chance that separate trees confuse one another. The changes also make child-process host objects reference-counted so they can be safely kept alive while in use.

features.summary: The `EXT_texture_norm16` WebGL extension test is now limited to WebGL 2, matching the API version that exposes the feature. This prevents the test from incorrectly treating it as available in WebGL 1.

features.summary: The graphics team cleaned up how Glean, Firefox’s telemetry system, describes its metrics by removing references to subsessions. This keeps the metrics definitions clearer without changing a visible browser feature.

features.summary: The WebGPU bindings now enforce a Rust safety rule that requires potentially unsafe operations to be marked clearly. This helps catch risky code during development; it does not add a new WebGPU feature for users.

These changes help complex pages and graphics render more reliably and smoothly.

features.summary: Image loading and decoding received fixes for multipart images and more consistent handling of request settings inherited from a load group. Firefox also avoids unnecessary image-URL processing when it is not collecting profiler or memory-report data, reducing overhead. A diagnostic note was added for a Windows shutdown case where a system icon call is still running.

features.summary: Firefox updated its WebGPU backend and improved how it reports device-creation errors and the limits a device actually supports. It also now restricts certain storage-buffer and storage-texture limits to the WebGPU specification’s binding limit, and fixes crashes in rendering paths that do not read results back to the CPU. These changes make WebGPU behavior more accurate and dependable for applications.

features.summary: Each graphics layer tree now has its own identifier space, reducing the chance that separate processes or windows confuse their layer resources. Firefox also adds support for running the GPU process in headless mode and reports Android graphics capabilities more clearly. These changes improve graphics-process coordination and support automated or display-free environments.

features.summary: Graphics tests now cover protected DRM video layers on macOS, image geometry validation, and drawing snapshots at the correct page zoom. Additional edge-case fixes prevent overflow in box-shadow and SVG tile calculations, making the test suite better able to catch rendering errors.

features.summary: Firefox’s OpenGL and EGL graphics paths were updated to work more reliably with shared graphics buffers, including Linux DMA-BUF surfaces used to exchange image data efficiently. The changes also address graphics-resource handling and synchronization on some Radeon systems, while removing an unused Android canvas path; these are behind-the-scenes improvements to stability and performance.

features.summary: Firefox’s WebGPU support was made more dependable when discovering which features a graphics adapter supports and when reporting device limits to websites. This helps WebGPU apps receive accurate capabilities and avoid unexpected failures; a small internal cleanup also improves how shader constants are matched.

features.label: Image decoders

patches.author: Timothy Nikkel
patches.subject: Bug 2079663. Don't premultiply JXL images that have premultiplied alpha a second time.

patches.subject: Add a few SCHEDULES.exclusive rules for improved deterministic platform selection. DONTBUILD

features.summary: A fix prevents JPEG XL (JXL) images with premultiplied alpha from having their transparency applied twice, which could otherwise affect how the image’s colors appear. The remaining changes support more predictable platform selection during builds.

features.label: Image tests

patches.author: serge-sans-paille
patches.subject: Ensure correct usage of std::forward in image/

patches.author: Tim Elliott
patches.subject: Use libwebp scaled decoding to reduce WebP decode cost when downscaling.

patches.author: python273
patches.subject: Use paired nearest alpha rounding and correct conversion expectations.

features.summary: Image handling was improved so WebP images can be decoded at a smaller size when they’re being displayed smaller, reducing the work needed for downscaling. The accompanying fixes and tests tighten how image data is passed around and how transparency edges are rounded, helping keep results correct.

features.label: Colour management (QCMS)

patches.author: Timothy Nikkel
patches.subject: Bug 2083237. Add more info to about support about display color management profile.

patches.author: Timothy Nikkel
patches.subject: Bug 2081138. Remove the branches from qcms's clamp_u8.

features.summary: Firefox’s support information now gives more detail about the display color profile used for color management, making it easier to understand how colors are adjusted for a screen. A small QCMS optimization also streamlines conversion of color values to 8-bit channels.

features.label: Graphics core internals

patches.subject: Bug 2076516 Part 2 - Add fmt::formatter support for gfx and layout types.

patches.author: longsonr
patches.subject: optimise hue-rotate filter of 0

features.summary: Graphics and layout types gained support for clearer, consistent formatting, which helps when examining graphics information. Firefox also avoids unnecessary work for a hue-rotate filter set to zero, since it leaves the image unchanged.

features.label: Ipc

patches.subject: Fix handling of out-pointer parameter

patches.author: serge-sans-paille
patches.subject: Remove redundant idiom when using std::make_unique<T>(...)

features.summary: IPC (inter-process communication) handling was corrected for a function that returns data through an output pointer. The other change removes a redundant pattern in object creation, with no intended visible behavior change.

features.label: Rust

patches.author: Timothy Nikkel
patches.subject: Bug 2073543. Don't crash when jxl-rs can't build an ICC profile for the JXL output color space.

patches.author: Timothy Nikkel
patches.subject: Bug 2073321. Upgrade jxl-rs to 0.7.4.

features.summary: Firefox updated jxl-rs, its Rust library for decoding JPEG XL images, and fixed a case where decoding could crash if the image’s color profile could not be built. This makes JPEG XL image handling more robust for images with unusual or unsupported color-space details.

features.label: Graphics configuration

patches.author: Sotaro Ikeda
patches.subject: Enable WebRender layer compositor even when hardware stretching is not supported

features.summary: Firefox can now enable the WebRender layer compositor even on hardware that does not support hardware stretching. This lets more systems use that compositor path instead of requiring that particular graphics capability.

features.label: Graphics core

patches.author: KayanoLiam
patches.subject: Don't reference subsessions in Glean metrics files

features.summary: The graphics team cleaned up how Glean, Firefox’s telemetry system, describes its metrics by removing references to subsessions. This keeps the metrics definitions clearer without changing a visible browser feature.

features.label: Graphics core docs

patches.author: Nicholas Rishel
patches.subject: Add section for testing after vendoring ANGLE.

features.summary: The graphics documentation now explains how to test after updating ANGLE, the graphics library Firefox uses for translating graphics commands. This gives contributors clearer guidance for checking that such updates work as expected.

features.label: Image encoders
features.summary: A fix landed in Firefox’s image-encoding code. The patch title doesn’t say which image format or behavior changed, so there isn’t enough information to describe its user-facing effect reliably.

features.label: Remote

patches.author: Leo Tenenbaum
patches.subject: Fetching icon for Declarative Web Push.

features.summary: Firefox can now fetch an icon for Declarative Web Push notifications, so a notification can include its intended image. This helps notifications appear more recognizable when they arrive.

features.label: WebGPU tests

patches.subject: chore(webgpu): update CTS to a5e5d7440fa036b74ea13c3c5cb6b618a3c884e9

features.summary: Firefox updated its WebGPU conformance tests to a newer version of the WebGPU CTS, the test suite used to check that graphics features follow the standard. This brings the tests in line with the latest coverage and expected behavior.
